posts.author: Mdeyhim
posts.body:
Hello everyone. I know my join date says 2021, which is actually correct. When MZ came out, I got it and built a small series of maps/events. It let me know the capabilities of RPGMaker. I had looked into it before, but didn't like the level of options/features in the previous versions. While I thought about building a game and made the intro of one, I am better at writing than placing stuff on a grid. So, I shelved my idea of making a game. The time to completion was not worth it. I can write faster, and it is easier than making a game.
Skip ahead to 2025, I did an in depth dive into AI and using that to help build maps/tilesets. I can say with 100% confidence that it is completely and utterly impossible and probably will be until we are all replaced by robots and Skynet. Just like long form writing, there are some things AI just can't do. Tilesets in strict 48x48 px grids cause AI to have a literal meltdown, both chat focused AI and art focused AI. It is honestly surprising how bad AI is for something that would seem so simple. I know AI can't do long form writing, but I guess I owe an apology to the artists out there as well, since AI can't do RPGMaker art either and I thought it gotten to the point that it could. Don't get me started on even the most basic map layouts. Calling it mentally challenged when asked to make a text map of a forest village is being nice, having a bridge run parallel to river. Yes, parallel to a river, think about that for a moment. The dungeon generator in RPG Maker is actually better than all the AI out there, yeah...which isn't saying much. At least AI can make music like a boss.
Well, that is a quitter attitude, and I see a lot of potential in an RPGMaker game if done a certain way. So, after sitting down and really thinking hard about how to handle a workflow and quickly building maps, I am working on a game, like everyone else on this forum. Going to have to do things the regular way like everyone else in terms of map building at the base level, but I am looking at how I can cut down on the time building so I can rapidly build maps when I am ready to pull the trigger. Doing a lot of prep work ahead of time, and I mean a lot. The idea being that once I start building maps, I don't have to think too hard about each and every tile and look for tiles I need, since a lot of stuff will be prepped ahead of time. Going to do things in bite sized chunks, one map at a time, to see how things go and not burn out.
At least I have a killer music playlist to listen to for the themes of my main characters and antagonists. The goal being, that I should recognize them each separately purely by sound so there is enough differentiation. Right now, I am working through the map layouts and tileset requirements. Once I have a full enemy list and enemy skill list, then I need to set up an excel spreadsheet to start running test calculations, but that is much later on. Game mechanics is a fun problem to work on, writing and math are my strong points. Figuring out tileset and map layouts, not so much. Art is my critical weakness. I min maxed too much in real life.
Also testing the list of plug-ins I have picked out. There are so many options now for that kind of stuff it is honestly amazing. There is a plug-in for literally everything. Creating a story and iconic characters was the easiest part. Even figuring out key story themes or plot hooks was fairly simple. A lot of stuff you can do in RPGMaker that wouldn't work well as an actual story. The hard part is going to be mapping what I want. Events aren't too difficult once I get going on them. I just need to get some practice in RPGMaker event script again, but I am not worried. RPGMaker has a very intuitive event system, which is one of its most impressive features.
As for team ups or working with others, I want to test my workflow first and build the starting map and probably the next couple ones as well, first. I need to get a better idea of how fast I can actually work at map building. Talk is cheap after all, guess what thing AI does best ;p.
Well, this is me just saying hello.
